name: TANK Shanghai
funding: Founded by collector and karaoke-club owner Qiao Zhibing, who told The Art Newspaper he paid for it. The government-backed West Bund Group invited him and manages the surrounding park.
watch: Opened in March 2019 in five former aviation fuel tanks. Time Out says Qiao invested with West Bund Group; no budget was found.
records_note: Its site names a four-person council led by founder Qiao Zhibing; it posts no annual reports, accounts or funder list.

name: Istanbul Modern
funding: Founding sponsor Eczacıbaşı; main sponsor Doğuş Group with Bilgili Holding. The September 2026 sponsor panel lists Volvo, Visa, Mercedes-Benz, Nescafe, Paribu, TAV Airports and the Istanbul municipality.
watch: A December 2023 sit-in delivered over 5,500 signatures for full-day free entry and open data. Eight artists and a collective pulled works in 2011.
why_flagged: Founding sponsor Eczacıbaşı; main sponsor Doğuş Group with Bilgili Holding. The September 2026 sponsor panel lists Volvo, Visa, Mercedes-Benz, Nescafe, Paribu, TAV Airports and the Istanbul municipality.
records_note: It posts no annual reports or accounts; its sponsor page is one logo panel dated September 2026, and its administration page names the board.

name: Nasjonalmuseet (National Museum of Norway)
funding: State-funded foundation; 2024 income NOK 1,059M, gifts NOK 12.5M. Fredriksen Family Art Company lends its collection on a ten-year deal and funds four PhDs. AKO Foundation and Sparebankstiftelsen DNB give.
watch: June 2022 appeal urged ending the Fredriksen deal; critics cite Seadrill's 2014 Rosneft contract. The museum sees no reason for review.
why_flagged: State-funded foundation; 2024 income NOK 1,059M, gifts NOK 12.5M. Fredriksen Family Art Company lends its collection on a ten-year deal and funds four PhDs. AKO Foundation and Sparebankstiftelsen DNB give.
records_note: Annual reports run from 2003 to 2025, accounts are filed in the Norwegian register, partners are named without a date, and the board is listed.

name: Istanbul Biennial (İKSV)
funding: Run by İKSV. Koç Holding is main sponsor for 2007 to 2036. Its group includes oil refiner Tüpraş, almost half its revenue, and defence maker Otokar.
watch: Direnal-Istanbul protested Koç's sponsorship at the 2009 opening. In 2013 protesters wore Koç banners. The 2025 edition drew over 600,000 visitors.
why_flagged: Run by İKSV. Koç Holding is main sponsor for 2007 to 2036. Its group includes oil refiner Tüpraş, almost half its revenue, and defence maker Otokar.
records_note: Reports run from 2013 to 2025, the 2024 one with income and expense tables; Biennial sponsors are named and the trustees and directors are listed.

name: Borusan Contemporary
funding: Corporate museum of Borusan Holding, run by the Borusan Kocabıyık Foundation in the holding's headquarters. Group units: EnBW wind power, steel pipe, Caterpillar dealing, car sales.
watch: Opened in 2011 during the 12th Istanbul Biennial. Borusan EnBW Enerji runs 725 MW of renewable plants.
records_note: Names its Board of Trustees and staff; no annual reports, accounts or funder list are published, and its listed partners are service vendors.

name: Serendipity Arts Festival
funding: Non-profit Serendipity Arts Foundation, founded by Hero Enterprise chair Sunil Kant Munjal. 2025 partners include the Goa government, Hero Insurance Broking, Hero Realty, Campa, Milton and foreign cultural institutes.
watch: On 18 December 2019 the organisers shut two exhibits with CAA and NRC content, citing technical issues. Poets called it political suppression.
why_flagged: Non-profit Serendipity Arts Foundation, founded by Hero Enterprise chair Sunil Kant Munjal. 2025 partners include the Goa government, Hero Insurance Broking, Hero Realty, Campa, Milton and foreign cultural institutes.
records_note: It posts no reports, accounts or full trustee list; its patrons page names nine patrons undated, and the 2025 festival partners page shows only logos.

name: Dr. Bhau Daji Lad Mumbai City Museum
funding: Public-private partnership of the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai, the Jamnalal Bajaj Foundation and INTACH. The Corporation paid INR 2.8 crore for the 2025 reopening repairs.
watch: Mumbai's oldest museum; it reopened on 8 January 2025 after four years closed.
records_note: Names its Board of Trustees, chaired by the Mumbai mayor; no annual reports, accounts or donor list are published, only membership tiers.

name: Museum of Art & Photography (MAP)
funding: Private museum of the Art & Photography Foundation. Founder Abhishek Poddar gave the collection and his family the land. Building donors include Kiran Mazumdar Shaw, Sunil Munjal, Citi and Tata.
watch: In 2016 artists held a sit-in and a 1,000-signature petition against a state deal giving its parent foundation the Venkatappa Art Gallery.
why_flagged: Private museum of the Art & Photography Foundation. Founder Abhishek Poddar gave the collection and his family the land. Building donors include Kiran Mazumdar Shaw, Sunil Munjal, Citi and Tata.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2020-21 to 2025-26 and audited statements from 2014-15, names its trustees, and shows founding patrons only as logos.

name: Bengal Foundation
funding: Private trust founded in 1986, funded entirely by the Bengal Group. Chairman Abul Khair Litu co-founded AB Bank. It runs a fine arts gallery, a music festival and publishing.
watch: In July 2024 the Anti-Corruption Commission endorsed a charge sheet against Litu for acquiring about Tk 903 million in assets beyond his income.
why_flagged: In July 2024 the Anti-Corruption Commission endorsed a charge sheet against Litu for acquiring about Tk 903 million in assets beyond his income.
records_note: Names its Board of Trustees and says the trustees fund it; no annual reports, accounts or donor list are published.

name: Vasl Artists' Association
funding: Non-profit company limited by guarantee. Its 2026 disclosure lists COMO Museum of Art, Khurram Kasim Art Foundation, HUM TV, HBL Art Committee, Kadist, AFIELD and private collectors.
watch: Runs residencies and exhibitions in Karachi; over 500 artists have taken part in 25 years.
records_note: Names its board and supporters in a 2026 disclosure; posts no annual report, and says audited accounts exist but does not publish them.

name: Lalit Kala Akademi
funding: Autonomous body funded by the Union Ministry of Culture, founded in 1954. It runs the National Exhibition, the Triennale-India and seven regional centres.
watch: The government took over its management in April 2015, citing irregularities. A 2017 Delhi High Court petition claimed misappropriation of funds.
records_note: Posts annual reports for 2012-13 to 2018-19 and names its Executive Board; no audited accounts or funder list found.

name: Anadolu Kültür (Depo and Diyarbakır Arts Center)
funding: Founded 2002; runs Depo in Istanbul and the Diyarbakır Arts Center. Supporters named: Sigrid Rausing Trust, Civil Rights Defenders, Foundation for Arts Initiatives and Stiftung Mercator.
watch: Founder Osman Kavala has been jailed since 2017 and got a life sentence in 2022. Turkey neither funds nor controls the group.
records_note: Names its administrative board and four institutional supporters on the about page, undated; no annual reports or accounts are published.
